_provenance.does_not_license: Measures THIS repo's checked-in quality artifacts. Says nothing about a consumer repo's corpus. Evidence that arming costs this repo N, not that arming is free anywhere else. The refused artifacts are not all ones the default runner reaches -- the gate is normally handed latest.md only -- so 'would refuse 3 citations' is not 'would redden the next quality run'. Nothing was armed and no frozen artifact was rewritten.

first_executed_number_was_wrong.bias: one-way: it inflated marked and deflated the measured cost
first_executed_number_was_wrong.consequence: the buggy run supported 'the toll is smaller than D47 recorded'. Corrected, the artifact count moves 3 -> 4, closer to the hand count's 5 but still below it. Found by the round-1 bounded review before the number was trusted.
first_executed_number_was_wrong.what: the first cut of the marker test used `[^`]*field[^`]*`, which matches the GAP BETWEEN two adjacent code spans, so a bare English mention sitting between two unrelated spans scored as marked

_provenance.known_false_positives_not_repaired: `markers_for` treats a field name inside ANY backticked span as a citation, so a backticked PATH or flag containing the name as a hyphen-delimited token (`advisory-interpretation-contract.md`, `--paths`) scores as marked. Underscores are safe. Bias runs the same way as the repaired bug -- it inflates marked. Verified inert on today's corpus (those artifacts cite no inventory declaring that field), so the numbers above stand, but one new artifact quoting `--paths` while citing inventory_nose_clones.py would flip a refusal silently. Also unmodelled: lines with an odd number of backticks (a wrapped span's continuation line inverts code/prose -- zero live instances found) and fenced code blocks (pasted `status: ok` output scores a colon marker; fences exist only under --recursive). Marker attribution is per LINE, not per occurrence, matching the sibling's current line-granular 170. Raised by the round-2 bounded review and recorded rather than repaired: round 2 is the review cap.

_provenance.synchronized_reason: Refresh the pinned measurement whenever the checked-in quality corpus changes; the floor and marker rule remain measured rather than armed.
_provenance.units_matter: The hand count's unit was REVIEWS (5). This script's units are CITATIONS (an artifact-inventory pair) and ARTIFACTS. Top level: 3 refused citations across 2 artifacts. So on the hand count's own unit the executed number is 2, not 5; the two agree only if 'reviews' is read as 'citations', which the hand count did not say. Recorded because an earlier draft of D47 swapped the units to claim agreement.
_provenance.why: docs/deferred-decisions.md D47 recorded '51 of 169 mentions unmarked' and 'refuses 5 checked-in reviews' as HAND measurements. This is the executed replacement. The original 169 was NOT hand-derived -- the sibling floor measurement produced it -- which is why the 2026-08-01 run reported a presence-only total that reproduced it exactly. The current synchronized corpus measurement is 170.
